messages:
sara_support: FYI customer reported intermittent mTLS handshake failures to our Private control plane after they enabled a 'zero-trust edge' proxy at egress. Symptoms: lots of ClientHello retransmits, server gives TLS handshake timeout (526) and we see resets. They say it started when the proxy was rolled.
josh_eng: Can you paste the tcpdump/snippet and the control-plane fqdn/ip they hit? Also which deployment (eu-west-1 private control plane)?
sara_support: EU private control plane (control.eu.redwood-inference.internal -> 34.211.76.12). Customer attached a short pcap snippet, here's the relevant TCP/TLS lines they copied:
```
12:03:44.123456 IP client > 34.211.76.12: Flags [P.], seq 1:512, ack 1, win 64240
12:03:44.123457 TLSv1.3 ClientHello, length 512 (fragmented)
12:03:44.223789 IP client > proxy: TCP Retransmission
12:03:44.223800 IP proxy > 34.211.76.12: Flags [P.], seq 1:256, ack 1, win 32768
12:03:44.323900 IP 34.211.76.12 > proxy: RST
```
They also said the proxy rewrites SNI to a generic hostname and does TLS-inspect with an intermediate replacement cert.
ahmed_netops: :eyes: That pattern looks like TLS record fragmentation + the proxy reassembling differently. Many middleboxes that do TLS-inspect will rewrite the ClientHello or strip certain extensions (ALPN/SNI) which breaks some server-side SNI checks and causes our control-plane to drop early. Do we require ALPN or any specific extension for control-plane mTLS? (we do use ALPN for http/1.1 vs http/2 routing on the control plane)
josh_eng: We don't strictly require SNI for client cert mTLS auth, but the control-plane routing expects SNI for virtual host selection in many clusters. If SNI is removed/mangled our listener may reject the handshake path or pick wrong cert. Also fragmented ClientHello across IP DF/MSS boundaries can cause proxies to reassemble incorrectly.
mike_sre: Short actionable checklist for support to ask customer:
- capture full 3-way + ClientHello with `-s 0` and `-w` pcap (we need the pre- and post-proxy packets)
- try L4 passthrough (disable TLS-inspect) to confirm proxy is the cause
- if they need TLS inspection, configure proxy to preserve SNI and ALPN and avoid ClientHello rewriting
- as a temporary mitigation, add an allowlist rule by destination IP (not SNI/domain) for 34.211.76.12/32 and 34.211.76.13/32 and allow outbound TCP 443 -> verify if SNAT is in place

ahmed_netops: Quick examples for them to run:
```
# pcap capture (on client side before proxy)
sudo tcpdump -i any -s 0 -w /tmp/controlplane-mtls.pcap 'host 34.211.76.12 and port 443'

# if proxy supports passthrough, test with curl from a host behind proxy
curl -v --connect-to 34.211.76.12:443:34.211.76.12 https://control.eu.redwood-inference.internal/health --tlsv1.3 --cert client.pem --key client.key
```
sara_support: Customer tried domain allowlist (SNI-based) but said their proxy rewrites SNI to "edge.local" so that failed. They also reported intermittent NAT and ephemeral egress IPs which complicates IP allowlists.
josh_eng: If ephemeral SNAT is preventing IP allowlist, ask them to carve a static egress IP or a small prefix for control-plane traffic. Otherwise the other option is L4 passthrough for those destinations so the proxy doesn't modify TLS.
deploy-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-345 — mTLS control-plane handshake failures (assigned: mike_sre)

mike_sre: Proposed next steps (we should send this to customer):
1) Capture and share pcap with full handshake (we need the fragment boundary). Prefer a capture that shows client->proxy and proxy->control-plane.
2) Temporarily configure proxy to disable TLS-inspect for control.eu.redwood-inference.internal or enable SNI/ALPN preservation.
3) If 2 is not possible, have them NAT to a stable egress IP/prefix and allowlist that at their firewall for outbound L4 passthrough.
4) If they can, reproduce while we tail logs on the control-plane (we'll correlate by src IP + time). Provide the pcap and wall-clock times.
sara_support: I'll send a single-message checklist to the customer with the pcap command, curl test, and the IPs to try. I'll also ask them for a short snippet of the proxy config that shows TLS-inspect rules. Will update here once we get the pcap.
